projects.name: Basement Ledger
projects.description: 128 BPM A minor: a locked basement loop, a sub anchor under it, and one hollow Synth cell that never resolves.

projects.name: Rotary Hood
projects.description: 132 BPM C minor: loop-funk drive with an open hat pushing ahead of the beat and a dry acid answer cut short.

projects.name: Motorik Mile
projects.description: 130 BPM D minor: the krautrock motorik pulse on a drum machine — no swing, continuous eighth-note hats, and a block bass that never lifts.

projects.name: Purpose Signal
projects.description: 134 BPM F♯ minor: two modules only. The floor never moves, so a single high Synth figure carries the whole piece.

projects.name: Chrome Cell
projects.description: 130 BPM G minor: a pure rhythm study. Sixteenth-note hats with a hole on every beat, rim on the odd steps, and Euclid rings that never line up.

projects.name: Dial Tone Loop
projects.description: 125 BPM B minor: Berlin dub techno. The muted chord lands off the beat and goes straight to the returns — here the mix is the arrangement.

projects.name: Schaffel Grain
projects.description: 126 BPM D minor: the Cologne schaffel limp — swing at 54 against a straight grid, triplet delay, and a driven bass filling the gap.

projects.name: Jack Ledger
projects.description: 122 BPM F minor: the Chicago jack in four sounds — straight kick, clap on 2 and 4, open hat exactly off the beat, closed hat on every eighth.

projects.name: Deep Pocket
projects.description: 124 BPM A minor: a ninth-chord pad that never leaves, with a rim on the last sixteenth of every beat as the only clock inside it.

projects.name: Bucharest Tick
projects.description: 123 BPM D minor: rominimal. Swing 38 and humanize 16 push almost everything off the grid, and the FM tom lands twice in two bars.

projects.name: Filter Sunrise
projects.description: 126 BPM C minor: French filter house. One organ loop repeats unchanged and the master character does the lifting.

projects.name: Garage Slant
projects.description: 128 BPM G minor: two-step garage. The only displaced kick in the catalog, snare on the third beat alone, swing at 58.

projects.name: Sunday Organ
projects.description: 120 BPM B♭ minor: the slowest house tempo here. A sustained organ, a soft clap, and a low tom that breathes once every two bars.

projects.name: Tech Pocket
projects.description: 125 BPM E minor: a rolling 32-step bass with glide is the lead, and the drums stay out of its way — clap once per two bars.

projects.name: Selected Drift
projects.description: 96 BPM A lydian: no drums and two modules. A four-voice lydian Drone field holds everything while the Synth drops one slow phrase per cycle.

projects.name: Sequencer Field
projects.description: 92 BPM D minor: Berlin School. The sequencer is the rhythm — a three-octave sixteenth-note Arp over a deep Drone, with no percussion and no lead voice at all.

projects.name: Amen Chapel
projects.description: 168 BPM F minor: atmospheric jungle. A broken four-sound break against a pad moving at a third of its speed — the gap between the two is the piece.

projects.name: Autobahn Coast
projects.description: 108 BPM C minor: electro of the Kraftwerk line. Six displaced kicks per two bars, snare on the third beat only, and a square bass doubling the kick an octave up.

projects.name: Tilt Machine
projects.description: 112 BPM F♯ phrygian: nothing lands where you expect. Odd-step kicks, a late snare, hats grouped in threes, and humanize at 20 so it reads as played.

projects.name: Tape Haze
projects.description: 84 BPM D minor: the slowest project in the catalog. Halftime drums over a night Drone, with the Synth on maximum glide to imitate tape drag.
